subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: Should OpenClaw support Anthropic native server tools as a provider-owned opt-in feature, and what security/replay defaults should govern web_fetch and code_execution/PTC allowed_callers?
rationale: The useful request is not a narrow bug fix: it adds provider-specific config/API behavior, changes what data leaves OpenClaw, and may allow Anthropic-hosted code to invoke OpenClaw tools.

options.title: Design provider-owned opt-in server tools
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a staged Anthropic plugin/transport design with explicit defaults, server-block replay semantics, and security proof before implementation.

options.title: Land only a narrow web_search slice
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49949 as the canonical web_search-only path while leaving web_fetch and code_execution/PTC out of scope until separately approved.

options.title: Defer code_execution/PTC
options.body: Allow lower-risk web_search/web_fetch exploration but require a separate maintainer security decision before any allowed_callers or provider-hosted code execution support.

recommendation.title: Design provider-owned opt-in server tools
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a staged Anthropic plugin/transport design with explicit defaults, server-block replay semantics, and security proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest current issue-discussion and Anthropic transport/config history signal in the available evidence.
